title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E01 — A Meeting of Two Worlds
Introducing the themes of increasing American power; indigenous political aspirations; conflicting interests and goals; growing mutual antagonism; setting the stage for World War I.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E02 — Wilson & the Breakup of the Ottoman Empire
An examination of wartime and postwar American policy; showing how Wilson's commitment to an ethnocentrically defined view of national self-determination drives his efforts to shape the postwar settlement in the Middle East.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E01 — Uncovering Near Eastern Civilization
Egypt, Greece and Rome may be better known to the public; more written evidence survives from Mesopotamia; embarking on a journey through over 3,000 years of history; learning why Mesopotamia's rediscovery is so valuable.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E02 — Natufian Villagers and Early Settlements
The enormous value of plant and animal domestication; the theories about the transition from a hunter-gatherer lifestyle to agriculture; the challenges that farming presents; a perspective on the cultural sophistication of pre-agrarian peoples.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E01 — The Land of Canaan
What is meant by "holy land"; the difference between archeology and history; how reliable the Hebrew Bible is as a window into life in ancient Israel; answers to these and other questions; the region's earliest recorded inhabitants, the Canaanites.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E02 — The Arrival of the Israelites
What archeologists uncover about the arrival of the Israelites into Canaan; an ancient Egyptian stele with the earliest reference to Israel; the remains of Jericho's walls; a Philistine temple similar to the one Samson destroys in the book of Judges.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E01 — Biblical Israel - The Story of a People
Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E02 — By the Rivers of Babylon - Exile
A look at the Babylonian exile; the exiled Judeans begin asking themselves who they are as a people and why they are conquered; as the Bible begins to be compiled in this time of exile, it offers two vantage points for understanding its history.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E01 — Muslim Empires: Land, Language, Religion
The geographical region known as Greater Middle East; the range of nations and cultures that define it; historical turning points to witness, encompassing conquests, political alliances and Islam's rise; social, intellectual and economic reforms.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E02 — Muhammad and the Dawn of Islam - 622
Islam's rise is a major turning point; tracing key phases in the life of Muhammad (PBUH); the founding of the faith through his years of opposition; his establishment of Islam as a religious and political entity; the global impact of these events.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E01 — From Camels to Stars in the Middle East
One of the most important yet overlooked periods in human history; the who, what, why, where, when and how of the Golden Age of Islamic Civilization; exploring the Abbasid Empire; how it bridged the ancient world and the Renaissance.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E02 — Ibn Battuta's Search for Knowledge
Meeting the Moroccan wayfarer Ibn Battuta; tracing his journey across Northern Africa and the Middle East in the century after the Mongol sack of Baghdad; new insights into the era, including whether it ever truly come to an end.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E03 — The Pauline Epistles
This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E04 — The Problem of Pseudonymity
This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E03 — Neolithic Farming, Trading, and Pottery
Travel is dangerous but people transport valuable goods, perhaps via chains of merchants; daily life in Neolithic Mesopotamia, where homes and villages reflect a simple society; evidence of intricate pottery shows that people care about aesthetics.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E04 — Eridu and Other Towns in the Ubaid Period
The Ubaid people construct monumental buildings, standardize some measurements and must have some sort of formal leadership to care for and control their populations; the people of the Ubaid coordinate their efforts to develop irrigation systems.

description:

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E03 — Arabian Nights Caliph: Harun al-Rashid
Getting to know Caliph Harun al-Rashid; Baghdad's House of Wisdom, which is the largest depository of books in the world at the time; it serves as the engine that drives much of the Golden Age; the Arabian Nights collection of stories and legends.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E04 — The Arab World's Greatest Writer: al-Jahiz
Considered by many scholars to be the finest writer of Arabic prose to ever live, Al-Jahiz is a stylist and author of more than 200 works, uncovering the origins of Arabic writing and documenting the life and works of Al-Jahiz.

description:
S01 E03 — Jerusalem - An Introduction to the City
Surveying the topography and layout of Jerusalem; reviewing biblical accounts of Jerusalem from the arrival of David around 1,000 B.C.E. to the start of the Babylonian exile in 586 B.C.E.; the remains of an Assyrian siege on the city of Lachish.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E04 — The Jerusalem of David and Solomon
A first look at the biblical City of David; combing through the remains of a scribe's house behind a city wall; the development of biblical Hebrew script; rare examples of this script in a clay sealing, a piece of pottery and a victory stele.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Creation Stories and Why They Matter
Considering the nature of creation stories.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Reading Metaphor in Creation Stories
Metaphor and symbol are integral to creation stories, as they form a crucial part of the language of myth.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Mesopotamian Creation: Enuma elish
Enuma Elish, also called the Seven Tablets of Creation, is a masterpiece of Mesopotamian literature.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — The Mesopotamian Flood: The Atrahasis Epic
Examining key Mesopotamian texts referencing a catastrophic flood which decimates humanity.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — Egyptian Gods of Creation
Take account of funerary texts that contain allusions to the ancient Egyptian conceptions of creation.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E06 — Egyptian Approaches to Creation
Within ancient Egyptian culture, explore the means by which the gods created the world and humanity.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E07 — The Storm God's Supremacy in the Baal Cycle
This ancient Syrian text, though it lacks an overt description of creation, resonates with key themes of other creation stories of the ancient Near East.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E08 — Hittite Creation in the Kumarbi Cycle
Here, encounter the Hurrians and Hittites, two lesser known but important peoples of the ancient Near East.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E01 — A Meditation on Empire
What makes a true "empire"; how empires rise and flourish; how they decline and fall; discovering pointed answers to these and other fundamental questions about the study of empires.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E02 — Lands, Seas, and Sources
The geography of the ancient Near East plays a decisive role in the region's fascinating empires; looking at the kinds of archeological and documentary evidence like discoveries from excavations of ancient sites help in understanding the period.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E03 — Sargon and the Dawn of Empire
Charting the rise and the eventual fall of the Akkadian Empire, established by Sargon and strengthened by his grandson, Naram-Sin; learning how they forged the administrative pattern that future Mesopotamian empires follow, pivoting the king.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E04 — The Third Dynasty of Ur
Professor Dise discusses the brief rise and the eventual disintegration of the imperial dynasty of Ur III in Sumer in the late 22nd century B.C., analyzing how the dynasty's ruler Ur-Nammu introduced tyrannical taxes and economic systems.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E05 — The Empire of Hammurabi
King Hammurabi fills in the power vacuum left in Mesopotamia after Ur III; establishing the First Dynasty of Babylon, he administers rule through a detailed code of law; the First Dynasty swiftly collapses after Hammurabi's death.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E06 — Mitanni and the Kassites
Investigating the histories of two Mesopotamian empires that emerged after the First Dynasty of Babylon; the Mitanni of the north follows a decentralized state, like a feudal society; the Kassites in the south bring about socio-economic changes.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E07 — The Rise of Hatti
The first Near Eastern empire expanding beyond the river valleys of the Nile and Mesopotamia is Hatti, the Hittite kingdom. It originated in the early second millennium B.C. Anatolia, facing crises that threatened its stability.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E08 — The Government of Hatti
Focusing on the elements of the Hittite government and paying particular attention to the central role played by the Great King in judicial matters, Hatti's intricate imperial system blends hierarchy, bureaucracy and feudalism.

S01 E06 — Mitanni and the Kassites
Investigating the histories of two Mesopotamian empires that emerged after the First Dynasty of Babylon; the Mitanni of the north follows a decentralized state, like a feudal society; the Kassites in the south bring about socio-economic changes.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E07 — The Rise of Hatti
The first Near Eastern empire expanding beyond the river valleys of the Nile and Mesopotamia is Hatti, the Hittite kingdom. It originated in the early second millennium B.C. Anatolia, facing crises that threatened its stability.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E08 — The Government of Hatti
Focusing on the elements of the Hittite government and paying particular attention to the central role played by the Great King in judicial matters, Hatti's intricate imperial system blends hierarchy, bureaucracy and feudalism.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Creation Stories and Why They Matter
Considering the nature of creation stories.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Reading Metaphor in Creation Stories
Metaphor and symbol are integral to creation stories, as they form a crucial part of the language of myth.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Mesopotamian Creation: Enuma elish
Enuma Elish, also called the Seven Tablets of Creation, is a masterpiece of Mesopotamian literature.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — The Mesopotamian Flood: The Atrahasis Epic
Examining key Mesopotamian texts referencing a catastrophic flood which decimates humanity.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — Egyptian Gods of Creation
Take account of funerary texts that contain allusions to the ancient Egyptian conceptions of creation.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E06 — Egyptian Approaches to Creation
Within ancient Egyptian culture, explore the means by which the gods created the world and humanity.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E07 — The Storm God's Supremacy in the Baal Cycle
This ancient Syrian text, though it lacks an overt description of creation, resonates with key themes of other creation stories of the ancient Near East.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E08 — Hittite Creation in the Kumarbi Cycle
Here, encounter the Hurrians and Hittites, two lesser known but important peoples of the ancient Near East.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E01 — A Meditation on Empire
What makes a true "empire"; how empires rise and flourish; how they decline and fall; discovering pointed answers to these and other fundamental questions about the study of empires.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E02 — Lands, Seas, and Sources
The geography of the ancient Near East plays a decisive role in the region's fascinating empires; looking at the kinds of archeological and documentary evidence like discoveries from excavations of ancient sites help in understanding the period.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E03 — Sargon and the Dawn of Empire
Charting the rise and the eventual fall of the Akkadian Empire, established by Sargon and strengthened by his grandson, Naram-Sin; learning how they forged the administrative pattern that future Mesopotamian empires follow, pivoting the king.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E04 — The Third Dynasty of Ur
Professor Dise discusses the brief rise and the eventual disintegration of the imperial dynasty of Ur III in Sumer in the late 22nd century B.C., analyzing how the dynasty's ruler Ur-Nammu introduced tyrannical taxes and economic systems.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E05 — The Empire of Hammurabi
King Hammurabi fills in the power vacuum left in Mesopotamia after Ur III; establishing the First Dynasty of Babylon, he administers rule through a detailed code of law; the First Dynasty swiftly collapses after Hammurabi's death.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E06 — Mitanni and the Kassites
Investigating the histories of two Mesopotamian empires that emerged after the First Dynasty of Babylon; the Mitanni of the north follows a decentralized state, like a feudal society; the Kassites in the south bring about socio-economic changes.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E07 — The Rise of Hatti
The first Near Eastern empire expanding beyond the river valleys of the Nile and Mesopotamia is Hatti, the Hittite kingdom. It originated in the early second millennium B.C. Anatolia, facing crises that threatened its stability.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E08 — The Government of Hatti
Focusing on the elements of the Hittite government and paying particular attention to the central role played by the Great King in judicial matters, Hatti's intricate imperial system blends hierarchy, bureaucracy and feudalism.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E01 — Touring the Cradle of Western Civilization
The dynamic civilizations that emerge in the Aegean; the scope of the human drama that is played out there; some of the towering figures and remarkable sites to encounter; Professor Hale's recommendations for traveling this world as the ancients did.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E02 — Athens - Around the Acropolis and Parthenon
The Acropolis is a symbol of Athens; the path of the ancient annual procession honoring Athena; the history and meanings of the site's iconic buildings; the superlative architectural features of the Parthenon and its surprising original uses.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E03 — In the Footsteps of Socrates - Historic Athens
Treasures surrounding the Acropolis; the Theater of Dionysos, where one ponders the rituals of early dramatic festivals; the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, a venue of music and recitations; the Pnyx, an ancient hilltop assembly point; the agora market.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E04 — Around Attica - Temples and Mysteries
Visiting sacred monuments of Greece's beautiful Attica region; the Amphiareion is a shrine of a prophet deity; ancient oracle and healing practices; imposing shrines to Artemis and Poseidon; Eleusis is the site of mystical religious rituals.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E05 — Seeking the Good Life - Corinth to Epidauros
Peloponnese is Greece's southern half; Greece's important sanctuary to Poseidon, where ancient athletes compete to honor the god; Corinth's acropolis and agora; the great healing center of Epidaurus; the best-preserved theater of the ancient world.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E06 — Mycenae - Where Kings Planned the Trojan War
The citadel of Mycenae is made famous in Homer's "Iliad"; the imposing Lion Gate; the rulers of Mycenae and ancient life in the citadel; key monuments; the extraordinary shaft graves of an early dynasty; the Megaron palace; the tomb of King Atreus.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E07 — Around Nafplio - Greek History at a Glance
Walking the fortress of Tiryns in Greece's Argolid region; Mycenaean and classical-age warrior culture; visiting the Heraion; the Roman villa of Herodes Atticus; the port of Nafplio, with its remnants of Venetian, Byzantine and Ottoman culture.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E08 — Ancient Olympia - Gods, Games, and Temples
Investigating the practices and culture of the original Olympic Games at sites including the palaestra, the stadium and the Temple of Hera; the heat and drama of the contests; the mindset of the competitors; athletic competition as worship.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E01 — Westward the Course of Empire
Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E02 — The West in the Colonial Era
Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E03 — Venturing Beyond the Appalachians
After the Revolutionary War, the land between the Appalachians and the Mississippi becomes part of the new republic; how the territory is organized; the Northwest Ordinance of 1787 creates a new set of rules that clashes with old realities.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E04 — Discoveries of Lewis and Clark
The journey of the two explorers who map the Louisiana Purchase between 1804 and 1806; how Lewis and Clark fit into the tradition of explorers looking for a water route to the Pacific; the political and geographic history of the Louisiana Purchase.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E01 — The Interconnected Earth
An overview of the unifying idea of Earth system science; this approach views Earth as an integrated network comprising the lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere; sampling the complex interactions between these realms.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E02 — The Vast Depths of Earth Time
Pondering how the great antiquity of Earth is discovered; the observations that lead to the concept of deep time; in the process, they develop the tools that can read the story in rocks; ending with an analogy that puts human time into perspective.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E03 — Fossil Clocks
Delving into biostratigraphy, the study of fossil sequences in rock strata; its discovery solves the problem of correlating sedimentary strata from different regions; this leads to the geological timescale, initiating a revolution in Earth science.

title: A New History of Life
description:
S01 E04 — Paleontologists as Detectives
How paleontologists interpret fossils to reconstruct the traits and environments of extinct life forms; some of the pitfalls of the field; these include cultural biases that can lead to doubtful conclusions, such as that of the Tyrannosaurus rex.

title: The History of the United States Navy
description:
S01 E01 — The British Origins of the US Navy
Exploring the British Royal Navy during US independence, delving into the lives of officers and sailors, facing harsh realities at sea.

title: The History of the United States Navy
description:
S01 E02 — American Revolution on River, Lake, and Sea
Witnessing Lake Champlain's shipbuilding, the birth of the Continental Navy, and John Paul Jones' exploits. Exploring privateering's role in the conflict.

title: The History of the United States Navy
description:
S01 E03 — Alexander Hamilton and the Early Navalists
Tracing disputes over a standing US Navy; Discover threats to American merchants and the Department of the Navy's creation.

title: The History of the United States Navy
description:
S01 E04 — British Blockade and the War of 1812
Investigating economic and political conflicts led to the US declaring war on Britain in 1812; Explore key naval battles and their strategic impact.

title: The History of the United States Navy
description:
S01 E05 — Pirates of the Barbary Coast and Caribbean
After initially combatting piracy, Witnessing the Navy's ongoing efforts against privateering and piracy following the conclusion of the War of 1812.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E01 — America Enters the War
U.S. Marines arrive in June 1965 to protect a U.S. air base; the North Vietnamese Army and the southern Viet Cong guerrillas launch attacks.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E02 — French Indochina and the Viet Minh
Surveying the economic exploitation and repression that defines Vietnam in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E03 — Dien Bien Phu and Vietnam Divided, 1953-1959
Examining mid-century Vietnam from the First Indochina War to the October 1955 referendum.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E04 — Five Leaders Who Defined the Vietnam War
Explore the makings of war in Vietnam through five major players, starting with Vietnamese leaders Hồ Chí Minh and Lê Duẩn in the north and Ngo Dinh Diem in the south.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E05 — The Rise of the Viet Cong, 1959-1962
Examining why the northern Vietnamese government decided to wage guerilla war in the south, and how it's adversaries responded.

title: America and the World: A Diplomatic History
description:
S01 E01 — Achieving Independence
Examining various themes, including isolationism, mission, expansionism, idealism, and realism; their origins in American history; their importance; their apparent contradictions; the Revolutionary War.

title: America and the World: A Diplomatic History
description:
S01 E02 — Confederation and the Constitution
The postwar United States consisting of sovereign, weak states gather into a loose confederation and live a threatened existence; examining those threats; the creation of the Constitution; establishing a stronger form of government.

title: America and the World: A Diplomatic History
description:
S01 E03 — The Great Debate-Jefferson versus Hamilton
The French Revolution and resulting European war produces foreign policy crises for George Washington; two fundamentally different policy recommendations; the partisan debate threatens to rip the nation apart; Washington's Farewell Address.

title: America and the World: A Diplomatic History
description:
S01 E04 — From the Farewell Address to the Quasi War
Washington's Farewell Address is one of the most misunderstood documents in American history; exploring Washington's intent; the politically courageous presidency of his successor, John Adams.

title: America and the World: A Diplomatic History
description:
S01 E05 — Jefferson and the "Empire of Liberty"
Thomas Jefferson's ideas regarding territorial expansion and its relationship to liberty become a dominant American force; Jefferson's attempts to implement them, including the Louisiana Purchase of 1803; this doubles the size of the United States.

title: America and the World: A Diplomatic History
description:
S01 E06 — The "Second War for Independence"
Attempts by Jefferson and his successor, James Madison, to use peaceful economic coercion to defend American neutrality fail to prevent a second war with England; how the War of 1812 produces numerous gains for the United States.
